question: How much factual and commonsense relational knowledge do off-the-shelf pretrained language models already store, without fine-tuning, compared with knowledge bases built by supervised extraction?
hypothesis: Pretrained language models may store relational knowledge from training data and be able to answer fill-in-the-blank cloze queries.
contributions: The LAMA (LAnguage Model Analysis) probe: cloze statements built from Google-RE, T-REx, ConceptNet and SQuAD facts
A systematic comparison of six pretrained LMs against RE-based knowledge bases and DrQA, without fine-tuning
Analysis of which fact types are recalled (1-1 vs N-M relations) and how sensitive recall is to query phrasing

method.summary: Facts (subject-relation-object triples or QA pairs) are turned into cloze statements with a hand-written template per relation. Each pretrained LM, untouched, ranks the masked single-token object over a shared ~21K-token vocabulary, scored by mean P@k. Baselines are a frequency ranker, a relation-extraction KB (naive and oracle entity linking) and DrQA.
method.task: cloze-style fact recall / probing of pretrained LMs; open-domain QA on cloze SQuAD

datasets.name: Google-RE
datasets.source: Google relation-extraction corpus, manually extracted from Wikipedia; each fact manually aligned to a Wikipedia text
datasets.preprocessing: Only place of birth, date of birth, place of death kept; other two dropped for multi-token objects. One manual template per relation, e.g. '[S] was born in [O]'

datasets.name: T-REx
datasets.size: 34039 facts, 41 Wikidata relations, at most 1000 facts per relation
datasets.source: Subset of Wikidata triples from T-REx (Elsahar et al., 2018); automatically aligned to Wikipedia (97.8% alignment accuracy reported by Elsahar et al.)

datasets.name: ConceptNet
datasets.preprocessing: OMCS sentence containing subject and object found, object masked and sentence used as template; one random sentence if several

datasets.name: SQuAD (cloze subset)
datasets.source: SQuAD dev, context-insensitive questions with single-token answers
datasets.preprocessing: Questions rewritten manually as cloze statements

models.name: RE (Sorokin and Gurevych, 2017)
models.architecture: LSTM encoder with attention, pretrained on a Wikipedia subcorpus annotated with Wikidata relations

other.variants: REn naive string-match entity linking; REo oracle entity linking

models.name: DrQA
models.architecture: TF/IDF retrieval of top k articles then neural reading comprehension; constrained to single-token answers

inference.decoding: Rank every token of the shared vocabulary by the model's softmax output at the masked position; single-token objects only. Unidirectional: output just before the token; ELMo: average of forward and backward softmax; BERT: masked-token output.
inference.samples: One deterministic ranking per fact; no seeds or repeated runs reported. Phrasing-sensitivity test: max 100 random facts per relation, 10 random aligned Wikipedia sentences each (facts with fewer than 10 alignments excluded).
inference.prompting: Manually defined cloze template per relation; zero-shot, no fine-tuning, object slot only
inference.retrieval: None for the LMs. DrQA baseline uses TF/IDF retrieval over Wikipedia (k not stated).

parameters.shared_vocabulary: ~21K case-sensitive tokens (intersection of all model vocabularies)
parameters.candidate_filtering: other valid objects from training data removed from candidates when ranking (Bordes et al., 2013)

metrics.name: mean P@k
metrics.definition: Per fact 1 if the gold object is in the top k ranked tokens, else 0; averaged per relation, then mean across relations

baselines: Freq (rank by object frequency per relation in test data)
eval.protocol: Per-relation P@k with mean across relations; no significance tests or seeds reported.

availability.weights: uses public pretrained checkpoints (fairseq, AllenNLP ELMo, Hugging Face PyTorch-Transformers)
availability.data: LAMA probe released in the repo above

limits: One manually written template per relation; the authors say this makes results a lower bound and want to quantify variance across templates.
Single-token answers only; multi-token answers left as an open challenge.
BERT may succeed from co-occurrence rather than understanding, and Google-RE sentences are likely in its Wikipedia training data.
Models differ in training data, so the study does not compare architectures or objectives for capturing knowledge.
GPT-1 and GPT-2 excluded (limited vocabulary, large model not public).
No seeds or variance reported; mean P@1 is an unweighted mean across relations.

terms.definition: a set of knowledge sources, each comprised of a set of facts, converted to cloze statements to test LMs
a pretrained language model knows a fact (subject, relation, object) if it can successfully predict masked objects in cloze sentences expressing that fact
